limitations_and_boundaries: The current model does not account for how the pattern is cemented once initiated.
The study exploits the simplicity of symmetry breaking in one dimension; future extensions needed for two-dimensional pattern emergence.
Investigations of pattern emergence in two dimensions across a tissue field are needed to address whether this mechanism explains follicle patterning during mammalian skin development.

incorrect_items.description: The extracted result states '250 µM ribose leads to fewer aggregates; 500 µM ribose abolishes observable aggregation', but the source excerpt uses mM, not µM: 'at a concentration of 250 mM ribose, fewer aggregates emerge, and treatment with 500 mM ribose abolishes observable aggregation'.

missed_core_items.description: The ex vivo reconstitution recapitulates the spontaneous formation of ordered aggregates observed in the skin, with progressive segregations of both cells and ECM.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: When tracking cell arrangement over time, we ﬁnd our ex vivo reconstitution recapitulates the spontaneous formation of ordered aggregates observed in the skin (Figures 2C and S2; Video S1). These appear as progressive segregations of both the cells and the ECM (Figures 2C and 2D; Video S2), recapitulating the coupling between the cells and the ECM in vivo.

missed_core_items.description: The ex vivo system demonstrates that dermal cells autonomously generate an ordered pattern of aggregates without cues from the epidermis.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: These results demonstrate that dermal cells autonomously generate an ordered pattern of aggregates without the requirement of cues from the epidermis, as previously suggested (Ho et al., 2019).

missed_core_items.description: A chick embryo fibroblast cell-line fails to properly form a pattern, highlighting the specificity of the patterning program and the importance of using fresh primary cells.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Importantly, not all types of ﬁbroblasts tested in this culture system undergo such transitions in our ex vivo platform. In particular, a chick embryo ﬁbroblast cell-line fails to properly form a pattern (Figure S2), highlighting the speciﬁcity of this patterning forming program and the importance of using fresh primary cells to model an in vivo process.

missed_core_items.description: Contractility is necessary for cell-ECM alignment: blebbistatin treatment prevents orientation of nuclei and fibronectin.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Indeed, we ﬁnd that when contractility is decreased through myosin II inhibition, nuclei and ﬁbronectin fail to orient (Figures 4A and 4B).

missed_core_items.description: Increasing ECM cross-linking with ribose significantly delays alignment.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: We ﬁnd that when we increase cross-linking of the collagen gel substrate through ribose-mediated glycation (Francis-Sedlak et al., 2009; Mason and Reinhart-King, 2013; Vicens-Zygmunt et al., 2015), alignment is signiﬁcantly delayed (Figures 4C and 4D).

missed_core_items.description: Cells from later ex vivo time points are more contractile: reseeded cells from 25 h initiate aggregation almost immediately, while those from 6 h take significantly longer.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Speciﬁcally, those reseeded from the late time point initiated aggregation almost immediately, whereas those from the early time point took signiﬁcantly longer, indicative of cells from later ex vivo time points being more contractile (Figure 4F).

missed_core_items.description: Cells isolated from later time points contract collagen gel more strongly in a collective traction force microscopy assay.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: In line with the above observations, cells isolated from a later time point contracted the collagen gel more strongly as compared with those cells isolated from an earlier time point (Figures 4G, 4H, and S3).

missed_core_items.description: Calcium oscillation frequency doubles from 12 to 32 h ex vivo.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Further, from 12 to 32 h, cells on average double the frequency of their calcium oscillations, which is consistent with a role for calcium in increasing contractility over time, ex vivo (Figures 5A and 5B; Doyle et al., 2004).

missed_core_items.description: Dermal cells on more cross-linked collagen gels have significantly increased Ca2+ signaling frequency compared to controls.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Indeed, we ﬁnd that dermal cells on more cross-linked collagen gels have signiﬁcantly increased Ca2+ signaling frequency as compared with controls (Figure 5C).

missed_core_items.description: The theoretical model predicts that the number of aggregates increases with contractile stress and decreases with hydrodynamic length; patterning timescale decreases with contractility and increases with hydrodynamic length.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Speciﬁcally, we ﬁnd that the number of aggregates that form should increase as contractile stresses generated by the cells increase, and patterning should take place within a shorter period of time. In turn, the model predicts that an experimental decrease of active cellular contractility would lead to fewer aggregates, which should form on a longer timescale. Moreover, an increase in the hydrodynamic length should lead to fewer aggregates and slower patterning.
